paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Faithfulness to God and faithfulness to people are the same road. Malachi starts with "Do we not all have one Father? Did not one God create us?" (Malachi 2:10). Then he asks why they break faith with one another, and every broken promise after that traces back to that question.

Look at what he says about the offerings. The people were covering the altar with tears, but the LORD no longer received their offerings gladly (Malachi 2:13). I think that hurts to hear, because the weeping was real. Still, a gift on the altar can't cover for a promise broken at home. God cares about how you treat the people you made covenants with, and He is a witness to every one of them (Malachi 2:14).

So what does it mean for you, baker? A promise is something God Himself sees, and He cares about it. The LORD says, "So guard yourselves in your spirit and do not break faith" (Malachi 2:16). Guard it on purpose, and keep your word to the people God has put right next to you. The story isn't over, and neither is the teaching.
